name: National University of Singapore
description: The National University of Singapore is a public research university founded in 1905 as the Straits Settlements and Federated Malay States Government Medical School, making it Singapore's oldest university. It is a comprehensive university with faculties spanning medicine, law, engineering, computing, business, science and the arts.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities and the country's largest, so it is the primary local benchmark against which overseas fees are compared.

programmes.name: Master of Computing (Computer Science Specialisation)
programmes.notes: Self-funded (not MOE Tuition Grant) programme. Total tuition of S$69,215 incl. 9% GST for the Aug 2027 intake (up to 40 Units), divided by the 1.5-year full-time candidature; the same fee applies to all nationalities. Citizen/PR: the programme page does not print a figure, but it is on NUS's list for the Master's by Coursework Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate (masters.nus.edu.sg; FAQ dated 3 Sep 2026), a 40% rebate for Singapore Citizens/PRs admitted in AY2024-AY2028, so the SC/PR figure is 60% of the published fee (S$41,529 incl. GST, /1.5). The 2026 history (total S$67,144) is a secondary figure, not confirmed on the official page, which now shows only the 2027 intake. No official source for the Aug 2024 or Aug 2025 intake fee could be found on 2026-10-01: the NUS Computing fee pages for every MComp track show only the 2027 intake, the Registrar's graduate fee PDF covers only MOE-subsidised programmes (MComp has been self-funded since AY2020/21), and web archives were unreachable, so no 2024/2025 rows are recorded. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees.

programmes.name: MSc in Finance
programmes.notes: Self-funded (not MOE Tuition Grant) programme. Whole-programme fee for the Aug 2027 intake (AY2027/28) on the official page: S$71,000 before GST = S$77,390 incl. 9% GST, same for all nationalities (NUS alumni get a 20% rebate). Citizen/PR: the page prints no SC/PR figure, but MSc (Finance) is on NUS's list for the Master's by Coursework Enhanced Tuition Fee Rebate (40% for SC/PR admitted in AY2024-AY2028; masters.nus.edu.sg, FAQ dated 3 Sep 2026), so the SC/PR figure is 60% of the published fee. Full-time takes about 12-16 months. The official page (mscfin.nus.edu.sg) still blocks bots (Incapsula challenge page to direct requests on 2026-10-01), so it was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. The 2026 history (S$75,210 incl. GST) is from a secondary site (educatly) and the SC/PR entries apply the same 40% rebate; the official page now shows only the 2027 intake, and no official page or PDF for the Aug 2024 or Aug 2025 intake fee could be found (web archives unreachable), so no 2024/2025 rows are recorded. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees.

programmes.name: Master of Laws (LLM, General)
programmes.notes: Tuition fees per annum for students matriculating in AY2026/27 from NUS Law's fee page ('LLM (General) / Corporate & Financial Services Law / International & Comparative Law / Intellectual Property & Technology Law' row). Citizen S$9,600 and PR S$17,050 are the MOE-subsidised rates, excl. GST (GST subsidised by MOE). International students are not MOE-subsidised: S$40,250 incl. 9% GST (a Singapore Citizen not taking the subsidy pays S$38,350). The specialist LLMs (Maritime Law, Asian Legal Studies, International Arbitration & Dispute Resolution, International Business Law) are self-funded at S$42,550 / S$38,940 incl. GST for all nationalities. A non-refundable acceptance fee of S$3,270 (incl. GST) is offset against tuition, so it is not a one-off fee. The page says fees are subject to change each AY; one-year programme. History (students admitted in August 2025) from the NUS Law 'Masters Programmes 2026' brochure PDF: S$9,600 / S$16,400 / S$37,100, confirmed by the Registrar's graduate fee PDF (gdtuitioncurrent.pdf, 'Updated as of June 2026'), whose cohort table 'Law' coursework row for students admitted in AY2025/2026 gives the same figures. 2024 history from the same Registrar PDF's cohort table for students admitted in AY2024/2025 ('Law' coursework row): SC S$9,600, PR S$15,750 (MOE-subsidised, excl. GST), international S$37,100 (incl. GST). Current figures also match the Registrar PDF's AY2026/2027 'Law' coursework row (9,600 / 17,050 / 38,350 / 40,250). Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees.

programmes.name: Doctor of Medicine (MD, Duke-NUS Medical School)
programmes.notes: Graduate-entry, four-year MD at Duke-NUS Medical School (a school of NUS). Annual tuition for students admitted in Academic Year 2026-2027, from Duke-NUS's 'Tuition Fees for Doctor of Medicine (MD)' section; the fees are MOE-approved and government-subsidised and are fixed for the four-year duration of study. Citizen S$50,050 and PR S$68,150: 'GST subsidy provided' (i.e. excl. GST, GST subsidised by MOE). International S$99,900: inclusive of 9% GST. All MD graduates serve a service commitment (bond) in the public healthcare sector: 4 years for Singapore Citizens, 5 years for PRs and international graduates. The NUS Registrar's graduate fee PDF refers readers to Duke-NUS's own site for these fees. duke-nus.edu.sg blocks bots (Incapsula), so the page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. Duke-NUS publishes only the current intake's fees (the FAQ and brochure repeat the AY2026-2027 figures), so no 2024 or 2025 history is recorded. Excludes Miscellaneous Student Fees, which Duke-NUS bills at the NUS graduate rates.
